footprint.note: E-078 §2: log2(footprint_km / 27.83) and log2(support_days / 5), clamped to +/-12; constant for this source but stored per row so every tier-P store reads identically

normalisation: RAW — not z-scored and not anomalised; the sampler standardises from training years only
platform_id: a numeric source id where the archive has one, else int(sha1(id)[:15], 16) — deterministic across machines and python versions, 60 bits, never negative

bin.npy.meaning: floor(time_s / 432000 s) — exact integer arithmetic; NEGATIVE before 1982 and kept

bin_offsets.npy.meaning: CSR: rows of bin b are [off[b - bin_first], off[b - bin_first + 1])

qc.npy.meaning: 0 not assessed, 1 good, 2 probably good, 3+ the source's worse grades

time_s.npy.meaning: seconds since 1982-01-01T00:00:00Z, negative before it; int32 spans 1913-12-13T20:45:52Z .. 2050-01-19T03:14:07Z and the builder refuses a row past it

values.npy.meaning: the channels below, RAW units, NaN = not measured

schema_version_note: schema 2 (family 10.1): the time column is `time_s`, int32 SECONDS since 1982-01-01T00:00:00Z. Schema 1 (family 10, family 8) carried `time_days`, float32 days, which resolves 21 s in 1993 and 84 s in 2024 — against slatrack's 1 Hz sampling, up to 316 consecutive samples shared a timestamp. `ml/family10_store.py` reads BOTH; only the time column changed, and the bins, footprints, channels and QC policy are identical.
